source.title: The Implicit Bias for Adaptive Optimization Algorithms on Homogeneous Neural Networks
source.authors: Bo-Han Wang; Qi Meng; Wei Chen; Tie-Yan Liu

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, including appendices, though some equations and figure details are flattened in extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests optimizer-dependent generalization and margin behavior using adaptive optimizers on natural labels, but uses margin theory and a narrow experimental setup rather than the original claim’s random-label memorization tests.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s own MNIST optimizer comparison, RMSProp epsilon comparison, and two-layer MLP initialization comparison. Theoretical results and cited findings are not rows. Figure-only values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The MNIST experiments measure held-out performance for adaptive optimizers and momentum SGD, bearing on V4. However, the supplied text states only comparisons among adaptive optimizers; the adaptive-versus-SGD ordering cannot be read from the flattened figures. Neither margin nor conditioner direction tests V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' interpretation but overstates the theorem as convergence to max-margin solutions. Under the stated assumptions, RMSProp and Adam without momentum have limit directions along KKT points of the L2 margin problem; AdaGrad instead has a conditioner-weighted problem that depends on its optimization history. These are not guarantees of globally maximal margin or superior test accuracy. The MNIST experiment reports worse test accuracy for AdaGrad than for RMSProp and Adam without momentum.
record.recipe_differences: Studies implicit bias in homogeneous networks under logistic or cross-entropy loss, comparing adaptive optimizer conditioner behavior and margin; it does not conduct random-label memorization tests.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer and RMSProp epsilon affect reported normalized margin and test generalization; AdaGrad’s conditioner direction and margin vary with initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: AdaGrad has lower MNIST test accuracy and lower final normalized margin than RMSProp and Adam without momentum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive optimizers can differ in held-out performance despite all reaching 100% training accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Smaller positive RMSProp epsilon produces smaller normalized margins and larger generalization error; epsilon zero fails to converge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RMSProp's generalization and convergence depend on its conditioner epsilon.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 100 initializations, AdaGrad's conditioner direction and margin vary, while RMSProp and Adam without momentum have coincident isotropic conditioner directions and smoother margins.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: AdaGrad's implicit optimization bias is more sensitive to initialization in this constructed task.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 139, 2021
record.problems: Experimental comparison is limited to MNIST and stated optimizer settings; exact plotted accuracy, margin, and epsilon values are not available in the supplied text. The constructed two-layer experiment reports training accuracy and margin but no held-out performance. The paper's theory concerns convergence direction and margin, not direct bounds on test error.
record.rows_left_out: No additional own-result rows omitted. Theoretical statements, cited prior results, and figure-only exact values were not entered as separate rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-versus-random-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error.
A systematic learning-rate and schedule tuning comparison; broader tuning against SGD; language benchmarks; decoupled weight decay; and switching from Adam to SGD.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbations, their correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.

missing.what: The held-out performance comparison between momentum SGD and each adaptive optimizer is not captured by the recorded directional result. Its ordering and size cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text, so no V4 verdict is justified.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the V7 support label: initialization-sensitive margins are not magnitude-aware sharpness. The stated adaptive-only and epsilon comparisons also do not justify the record's V4 scope-limit labels. The study is not an original source for any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No SGD versus adaptive-optimizer benchmark under broad or limited tuning; only one MNIST setup and the stated optimizer variants are compared.
No batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch large-batch test.
Does not test magnitude-aware sharpness, compare sharpness against other generalization measures, or use CIFAR-10/SVHN.
No example removal or retraining experiment.

rows.subject: homogeneous 4-layer convolutional neural network
rows.size_stated: 4-layer; 32 and 64 convolution channels; fully connected widths 1024 and 10
rows.operation_detail: Train with AdaGrad, RMSProp, Adam (w/m), SGD with momentum, and Adam with momentum; compare test accuracy and normalized margin.
rows.baseline: AdaGrad is the optimizer comparison reference; numerical baseline not stated.
rows.value: The paper states AdaGrad achieves lower test accuracy (worse generalization) than RMSProp and Adam (w/m); final normalized margin is lowest for AdaGrad. Figure-only accuracy values.
rows.note: Text explicitly describes the directional comparison; exact figure values are not given in the supplied text. The paper says all three reach 100% training accuracy.
rows.check: The experiment includes momentum SGD, but the recorded result compares AdaGrad only with RMSProp and Adam without momentum. That comparison cannot establish V4's adaptive-versus-SGD effect. Use momentum SGD as the relevant baseline and separate test accuracy from normalized margin. Learning-rate settings should follow Appendix F.1 rather than describe them uniformly as PyTorch defaults.

rows.subject: homogeneous 4-layer convolutional neural network
rows.size_stated: 4-layer; 32 and 64 convolution channels; fully connected widths 1024 and 10
rows.operation_detail: Train with RMSProp at different epsilon values and compare test accuracy and normalized margin.
rows.baseline: RMSProp with other epsilon values; numerical baseline not stated.
rows.value: The text states that as epsilon decreases, normalized margin gets smaller and generalization error gets larger; epsilon 0 did not converge.
rows.note: The supplied text gives qualitative trends only; exact epsilon values and plotted measurements are not recoverable.
rows.check: RMSProp's epsilon sensitivity measures held-out performance within one adaptive optimizer, without a comparison against SGD. It does not establish whether tuning removes or reverses an adaptive-versus-SGD difference. Epsilon-zero nonconvergence is a separate optimization outcome.

rows.subject: two-layer MLP Φ(x, w, v) = vσ(⟨w,x⟩)
rows.operation_detail: Train with AdaGrad, RMSProp, Adam (w/m), and SGD across 100 random initializations, then compare margin and convergent conditioner directions.
rows.measure: Training accuracy; margin and conditioner direction across runs
rows.baseline: RMSProp and Adam (w/m) conditioner directions coincide with each other and the isotropic direction; exact baseline value not stated.
rows.value: All optimizers achieve 100% training accuracy. AdaGrad margin fluctuates across initializations; RMSProp and Adam (w/m) margins are smoother. Figure-only margin values.
rows.note: The text reports initialization sensitivity and training accuracy, but provides no test error or test accuracy for this experiment.
rows.check: Training accuracy, margin variation and conditioner direction measure neither held-out optimizer differences in V4 nor magnitude-aware sharpness and generalization gaps in V7. The reported initialization sensitivity is clear, but its effect on held-out performance is not measured.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The reported test error and margin vary with epsilon, and training fails to converge when epsilon is removed (R2).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: AdaGrad across 100 random initializations on the constructed two-layer MLP task
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports that AdaGrad’s margin fluctuates across initializations and its conditioner direction is sensitive to initialization (R3), consistent with its account of an initialization-sensitive optimizer property; this is not a test of magnitude-aware sharpness or its correlation with generalization gap.
